newsitem.title: CHINA: China says HK need not worry over passports.
newsitem.headline: China says HK need not worry over passports.

text.p: China said on Thursday there was no need for Hong Kong holders of British passports to be worried over news they would not be entitled to consular protection by Britain after the colony's return to Chinese rule next year.
London this week jolted Hong Kong with an admission that it would not be able to protect local holders of British passports after Beijing regains control on July 1 next year.
"Although a small number of people are concerned about (this issue), I think (the concern) is unnecessary," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing in Beijing.

Cui repeated rules issued last May by the National People's Congress, or parliament, saying China would not allow British consular protection for holders of dual citizenship while they were on the Chinese mainland or in Hong Kong.

Britain's senior trade commissioner, Francis Cornish, said on Tuesday that London could not protect the more than 135,000 Hong Kong people granted full British passports, with the right of abode in Britain, under a special selection scheme in 1990.

Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Thursday called an urgent meeting of the Legislative Council to make a statement on the controversy, which his spokesman said had sparked considerable public interest and much misunderstanding.

In a concession to widespread demands for full British citizenship after Beijing's 1989 pro-democracy crackdown, London offered passports to 50,000 Hong Kong households, a privileged fraction of Hong Kong's 6.3 million people.
Cornish's remarks have been denounced by Hong Kong politicians as a sell-out by London.
